notes: An idle transaction's last statement needs Performance Schema with the events_statements_current consumer; MariaDB has both off by default.

MariaDB lists only the row locks involved in a wait (information_schema.INNODB_LOCKS). Locks that block nobody are not visible through SQL; rows locked and lock structs in the transactions table count them. MariaDB also shows record-only and next-key locks both as X, and gap and insert-intention locks both as X,GAP.

Rows a transaction inserted, and index entries its updates wrote, are protected by implicit locks, which InnoDB lists only after another session conflicts with them. A transaction can hold more locks than the list shows.

While a DDL statement such as ALTER TABLE waits for its exclusive metadata lock, new reads and writes of that table queue behind it, even when the lock the blocker holds (usually SHARED_READ or SHARED_WRITE from an open transaction) would let them through. One open transaction and one waiting DDL statement can stop every read and write of the table until the transaction ends or the DDL gives up after lock_wait_timeout (by default one year on MySQL, one day on MariaDB). Stopping the DDL statement (KILL QUERY on its connection) also releases the queue, but an ALTER TABLE stopped at its final step loses the work it has done and must run again.

MariaDB is not recording metadata locks here (Performance Schema and its wait/lock/metadata/sql/mdl instrument are off by default), so myflames cannot see exactly which session holds the table a DDL statement waits for. The likely blockers are open transactions, idle ones and ones that started before the DDL first: a transaction keeps the metadata locks of every table it used until it commits or rolls back. A transaction that started after a long ALTER TABLE began can also block its last step. Transactions that used only non-InnoDB tables (MyISAM, MEMORY, Aria) hold metadata locks too but are not in INNODB_TRX, so they are missing from this list. For exact blockers, add performance_schema=ON and performance-schema-instrument='wait/lock/metadata/sql/mdl=ON' under [mysqld] in my.cnf and restart, or install the METADATA_LOCK_INFO plugin (INSTALL SONAME 'metadata_lock_info'), which lists granted metadata locks. myflames changes neither.
